Earth Pulse
**An open-source, AI-powered explorer of how every place on Earth has changed over the last 40 years.**

chunks.title: Earth Pulse
chunks.text:
Earth Pulse
Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, challenge: *Be An Earth System Trend Detective*.
---

chunks.title: 1. The Idea
chunks.text:
1. The Idea
Click anywhere on the globe and instantly see how that place has changed: temperature, vegetation, rainfall, and sea level. Earth Pulse draws the long-term trend, forecasts the next few years, flags unusual events, and explains it all in plain English.

chunks.title: 1. The Idea
chunks.text:
1. The Idea
The signature feature is the **Opposite Trend Detector**: it finds neighbouring regions that are changing in opposite directions (one drying while the neighbour gets wetter) and explains why that can happen.

chunks.title: 5. AI/ML Layers
chunks.text:
5. AI/ML Layers
| Layer | Model | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Trend estimation | Theil-Sen slope, Mann-Kendall test | Robust long-term trend per grid cell |
| Forecasting | LSTM or temporal transformer | Predict the next few years |
| Anomaly detection | Autoencoder or Isolation Forest | Flag unusual events automatically |
| Clustering | K-Means or HDBSCAN | Find climate twins |
| Explainer | Local Ollama LLM (default `qwen2.5:1.5b`) + templated fallback | Turn pre-computed facts into plain English without inventing numbers |

chunks.title: 6. Architecture
chunks.text:
6. Architecture
- **Data layer:** download from Earthdata, clean with xarray, store as Zarr or NetCDF
- **Analysis layer:** Python with NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall, scikit-learn, PyTorch
- **API layer:** FastAPI serving trends, forecasts, and anomalies per location
- **Frontend:** React with MapLibre GL or Leaflet, plus Plotly or D3 for charts
- **Deployment:** one Render Docker web service (`render.yaml`) — FastAPI serves the built Vite app **and** the API from the same URL; GitHub Pages / Vercel / Netlify remain possible for the frontend only
Everything can run at zero cost. Free plans change, so check current limits.

This repository now contains a **working offline-first implementation** of the Earth Pulse stack (deterministic synthetic demo store; swap in real NASA products for research):

chunks.title: 14. What's implemented in this repo (v0.1.0)
chunks.text:
14. What's implemented in this repo (v0.1.0)
- **`pipeline/`** — sample store generator (`--sample`), NASA POWER point fetcher, GIBS tile builder, FIRMS fires (optional key), MERRA-2/MODIS/GPM OPeNDAP fetch path, CMR discovery, cleaning + feature engineering.
- **`engine/`** — Theil–Sen + Mann–Kendall trends for all grid cells, **Opposite Trend Detector** (NDVI/precipitation), K-Means **climate twins** → `data/processed/analysis.json`.
- **`models/`** — multivariate ridge-rollout forecaster with p10–p90 bands (real-POWER artifact `data/processed/forecaster_power_real.npz`, synthetic demo artifact `models/artifacts/forecaster.npz`; the loader picks the one trained on the same store distribution), transparent linear-trend fallback, rolling robust-z anomalies, rolling-origin backtest, dependency-free **SVG projected maps**, optional (disabled-by-default) AI scenario module.

chunks.title: 14. What's implemented in this repo (v0.1.0)
chunks.text:

Dockerfile for HF Spaces/Render free tier.
- **`web/`** — React + Vite + TypeScript frontend (**Leaflet** map, conversation-first UI, fact-locked Ollama chat, live coverage/forecast/opposite/twin/evidence cards, dark theme, localStorage dossier). In dev it proxies `/api` → `:8000`; in production the backend serves `web/dist` directly from the same origin. `cd web && npm install && npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000).
- **`docs/`** — architecture, data sources (with the honest 40-year coverage check), API contract, ML/accuracy notes, UI/UX spec, free deployment guide, parallel-session prompts.

chunks.title: Quickstart (offline)
chunks.text:
Quickstart (offline)
```bash
pip install numpy scipy fastapi uvicorn httpx pydantic pytest
make sample-data engine train test   # deterministic demo store → analysis.json → artifact → tests
make api                             # http://localhost:8000 (try /place?lat=12.97&lon=77.59)
cd web && npm install && npm run dev  # http://localhost:3000 (Vite proxies /api -> :8000)
```
`docker compose up --build api` runs the **single-service** image on :8000 (API + built frontend), or run native: `npm run build` in `web/` first, then `uvicorn api.main:app --port 8000` — same URL for the app and `/api/*`. `render.yaml` deploys that image to Render as one free Docker web service (`healthCheckPath: /api/health`); see `docs/deploy.md`.

chunks.title: Honest limitations
chunks.text:
Honest limitations
Bundled demo data is **synthetic** (physically motivated, deterministic). Real accuracy requires real products (`docs/data-sources.md`) and overlap-period training; forecasts are probabilistic (p10–p90), not certain futures. Never claim "40 years" for NDVI/SST/sea level (~2000/2002/1993 onward).

```json
"schema_version": "1.0.0",

"store": {
"path": "data/processed/earth_pulse_power_real.npz",
```

`POST /chat`
Conversational, facts-locked narration backed by the Hugging Face RAG Space (when `EP_RAG_BACKEND=hf`), a local Ollama model (default), or deterministic templated prose (fallback). The server assembles the facts (trends, forecast deltas, anomalies, opposite pairs, climate twin, coverage) from the same store and engine as `/place`; the model only re-words them and never computes or changes a number. With `EP_RAG_BACKEND=hf`, retrieval runs over a bundled BM25 knowledge base (repo docs + NASA POWER / method notes + store-derived coverage facts) and answers carry `sources: [{id, title, source}]`. Every draft passes the same post-generation guards regardless of backend.

chunks.title: `POST /chat`
chunks.text:
`POST /chat`
Request:
```json
{
"lat": 15.8497,
"lon": 74.4977,
"region_name": "Western Ghats + Arabian Sea",
"variable": "Precipitation",
"horizon_months": 60,
"language": "en",
"messages": [
{ "role": "user", "content": "What does the 5-year forecast say, and how uncertain is it?" }
]
}
```

chunks.title: `POST /chat`
chunks.text:
`POST /chat`
Response:
```json
{
"text": "The 5-year forecast indicates a net increase in temperature of +0.165 °C over 60 months …",
"generator": "ollama",
"model": "qwen2.5:1.5b",
"confidence": "medium",
"card_kind": "forecast",
"llm_available": true,
"guard_reason": null,
"guard_numbers": [],
"sources": [{ "id": "S1", "title": "Earth Pulse methodology", "source": "docs/rag-corpus/earth-pulse-method.md" }],
"facts": { "trends": {}, "forecast_deltas": {}, "parameters_unavailable": [] }
}
```
`guard_reason` and `guard_numbers` are always present; the latter is empty unless a numeric guard rejected a draft.

chunks.title: `POST /chat`
chunks.text:
`POST /chat`
Forecast deltas are **net change across the full horizon**, not per-decade rates. If Ollama is unreachable the endpoint returns deterministic `templated` prose instead of failing. Post-generation guards protect the facts: answers that convert a p-value into a certainty/probability claim, call a non-significant trend significant, or contain a number absent from the facts are rejected and replaced with `templated-guard` prose. `guard_reason` is one of `certainty_claim`, `p_value_misuse`, `band_misuse`, `significance_misread`, or `unverified_numbers`; `guard_numbers` lists any rejected numerical tokens (empty otherwise).

chunks.title: On-click data flow (Tier A — instant)
chunks.text:
On-click data flow (Tier A — instant)
1. User clicks `(lat, lon)` on the MapLibre GL map.
2. Frontend → `GET /place?lat=..&lon=..&horizon_months=60`.
3. API finds nearest grid cell, assembles: precomputed trends (Theil–Sen/Mann–Kendall), forecast (bundled model), anomalies (rolling robust z), opposite-trend pairs nearby, GIBS past imagery, POWER/FIRMS hints (Tier A), `data_coverage` provenance, plain-English narrative.
4. UI renders: coverage badge → charts (past + forecast with p10–p90 band) → past imagery gallery → optional data-driven projected map → Opposite Trend card → explainer.

chunks.title: On-click data flow (Tier A — instant)
chunks.text:
On-click data flow (Tier A — instant)
Tier B (`api/services/ondemand.py`) does bounded live discovery via CMR and caches; it is **opt-in**, never required for the demo, and never blocks Tier A.

chunks.text:
Data store formats
**Sample/demo (`data/samples/earth_pulse_sample.npz`)** — deterministic synthetic gridded multivariate series (see `pipeline/export_store.py`). Keys: `dates`, `lats`, `lons`, `grid_lat`, `grid_lon`, and one array per parameter `(T, G)`.

Data store formats
**Real-data path** — `run_pipeline.py --sample` (or `--gridded` for real Earthdata path) would write a consolidated Zarr store (`pipeline/export_store.py::export_zarr`) and the engine reads it with the same variable layout. The demo intentionally ships a tiny synthetic store so anyone can run the project offline.

Unified payload contract

chunks.title: Accuracy & honesty guarantees
chunks.text:
Accuracy & honesty guarantees
- Robust stats (Theil–Sen/Mann–Kendall) alongside ML — trends carry significance, not vibes.
- Forecasts are probabilistic: **p10/p50/p90**; UI never shows a single "certain" future.
- `data_coverage` reports which parameters/sources/years were actually used per place.
- Observed vs Forecast vs **AI-generated scenario** are visually distinct labels.
- The bundled demo data is **synthetic** (deterministic, physically motivated) and labeled as such everywhere; swap in real products for real analysis (`docs/data-sources.md`).

chunks.title: NASA (and partner) data sources — what to use, where to get it, how much history
chunks.text:
NASA (and partner) data sources — what to use, where to get it, how much history
Earth Pulse is built **only** on free, open data. This document lists every source,
what parameters it provides, how to access it, and — critically — **how many years of
history you can realistically get**. Coverage varies by variable; never claim "40 years
for everything" in the UI. Per-parameter coverage is surfaced in the app via
`data_coverage` (see `configs/params.yaml`).

chunks.title: NASA (and partner) data sources — what to use, where to get it, how much history
chunks.text:
NASA (and partner) data sources — what to use, where to get it, how much history
Legend: **access** = how the code fetches it · **history** = typical start of usable record.
---

chunks.title: 1. NASA Earthdata (hub) + Earthdata Search
chunks.text:
1. NASA Earthdata (hub) + Earthdata Search
- **What:** discovery + download for almost all NASA Earth-observation products (DAAC holdings).
- **Gives you:** virtually any gridded/remote-sensing variable, via CMR / `earthaccess`.
- **Access:** `earthaccess` Python API or direct OPeNDAP/download. Requires a **free Earthdata login** (set `EARTHDATA_USERNAME` / `EARTHDATA_PASSWORD`).
- **History:** product-dependent (see per-DAAC rows below).
- **Links:** https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov · https://search.earthdata.nasa.gov
- **In this repo:** `pipeline/auth.py` (login), `pipeline/discover.py` (CMR discovery), `pipeline/fetch_gridded.py` (OPeNDAP/xarray fetch).

chunks.title: 2. NASA Giovanni
chunks.text:
2. NASA Giovanni
- **What:** quick, interactive time-series and area-average analysis across hundreds of variables.
- **Gives you:** many of the same variables as time series/maps — ideal for **prototyping and validation**, not bulk production.
- **Access:** web UI; some service endpoints. Best used to sanity-check the numbers produced by this repo.
- **Links:** https://giovanni.gsfc.nasa.gov

chunks.title: 3. NASA GIBS / Worldview
chunks.text:
3. NASA GIBS / Worldview
- **What:** global **map tile layers** (near-real-time + historical), best for showing imagery on click and past views.
- **Gives you:** true color, corrected reflectance, NDVI/EVI layers, fires/thermal anomalies, aerosols, SST, snow/ice, precipitation, blue marble.
- **Access:** **GIBS WMTS** tiles, e.g. `https://gibs.earthdata.nasa.gov/wmts/epsg3857/best/<layer>/default/<date>/GoogleMapsCompatible_Level9/<z>/<y>/<x>.jpg|png`. No key.
- **History:** layer-dependent; most modern MODIS/VIIRS layers are ~2000+.
- **Links:** https://worldview.earthdata.nasa.gov
- **In this repo:** `pipeline/fetch_gibs.py` builds tile URLs; the frontend `LayerToggles`/`ImageryGallery` render them.

chunks.title: 4. LP DAAC (land) — via Earthdata
chunks.text:
4. LP DAAC (land) — via Earthdata
- **What:** land surface and vegetation.
- **Gives you:** **NDVI/EVI** (MODIS MOD13A3/MYD13A3), **LST** (MOD11A2), land cover, evapotranspiration (MOD16A2), burned area.
- **Access:** earthaccess/OPeNDAP, subset by bounding box or point.
- **History:** ~**2000–present** for MODIS (VIIRS continues post-2012). **Not 40 years.**
- **Links:** https://lpdaac.usgs.gov

chunks.title: 5. GES DISC (precipitation / atmosphere) — via Earthdata
chunks.text:
5. GES DISC (precipitation / atmosphere) — via Earthdata
- **What:** precipitation, soil moisture, atmospheric composition, aerosols.
- **Gives you:** **precipitation** (GPM IMERG V07; TRMM V7 before it), humidity, surface met fields, aerosol optical depth.
- **Access:** earthaccess / OPeNDAP; subset to monthly.
- **History:** GPM/IMERG **~2000–present** (stitch with TRMM 1998–2015 carefully). **Not 40 years** for the consistent record. MERRA-2 lives here too (see §11).
- **Links:** https://disc.gsfc.nasa.gov

chunks.title: 6. PO.DAAC (ocean) — via Earthdata
chunks.text:
6. PO.DAAC (ocean) — via Earthdata
- **What:** ocean physics — sea surface temperature, sea level, winds, salinity, currents.
- **Gives you:** **SST** (e.g., GHRSST MUR 0.01° daily), **sea-level anomalies** (satellite altimetry).
- **Access:** earthaccess / PO.DAAC APIs / OPeNDAP.
- **History:** SST MUR **~2002–present**; altimetry **~1993–present**. **Not 40 years.**
- **Links:** https://podaac.jpl.nasa.gov

chunks.title: 7. NSIDC (cryosphere) — via Earthdata
chunks.text:
7. NSIDC (cryosphere) — via Earthdata
- **What:** ice sheets, snow, sea ice.
- **Gives you:** sea-ice concentration/extent (Sea Ice Index / SMMR–SSM/I), snow cover fraction.
- **Access:** earthaccess / direct.
- **History:** sea-ice concentration **~1979–present** (product-dependent); snow cover similar; ice-sheet products vary.
- **Links:** https://nsidc.org

chunks.title: 8. NASA POWER
chunks.text:
8. NASA POWER
- **What:** agroclimatology / energy-oriented point time series.
- **Gives you:** **T2M (mean/max/min), precipitation, solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), relative humidity (RH2M), wind speed (WS2M), surface pressure (PS)** — queried for any lat/lon.
- **Access:** **POWER REST API, no key**, e.g. `https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/monthly/point?parameters=T2M&latitude=..&longitude=..&start=1981&end=2024&format=JSON`.
- **History:** ~**1981–present** (parameter-dependent; solar & met core are long).
- **Links:** https://power.larc.nasa.gov/data-access-viewer/
- **In this repo:** `pipeline/fetch_power.py` (Tier A on-click); sample demo also uses MERRA-2-style series.

chunks.title: 9. NASA GISS (GISTEMP)
chunks.text:
9. NASA GISS (GISTEMP)
- **What:** global surface air temperature anomaly.
- **Gives you:** monthly global & coarse-grid anomaly context.
- **Access:** published datasets (CSV), https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/.
- **History:** **1880–present**. Perfect for long-term context, not local full-field mapping.

chunks.title: 10. NASA FIRMS (fire hotspots)
chunks.text:
10. NASA FIRMS (fire hotspots)
- **What:** near-real-time active fire / thermal anomaly detections.
- **Gives you:** fire pixel detections (MODIS/VIIRS), fire radiative power.
- **Access:** FIRMS API with a **free map key** (`FIRMS_MAP_KEY`), e.g. `https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/api/area/csv/<key>/MODIS_NRT/<W,S,E,N>/<day_range>`.
- **History:** ~**2000–present**.
- **In this repo:** `pipeline/fetch_firms.py`; used as an anomaly/event signal, not a continuous climate field.

chunks.title: 11. MERRA-2 (NASA GMAO reanalysis, via GES DISC)
chunks.text:
11. MERRA-2 (NASA GMAO reanalysis, via GES DISC)
- **What:** the best **NASA backbone for 40+ years** of consistent multivariate fields.
- **Gives you:** 2m temperature, total precipitation, humidity, winds, radiation, pressure — consistently across **1980–present**.
- **Access:** earthaccess/OPeNDAP; monthly means (e.g., `M2TSMNXSLV`, `M2TMNXPER` collections).
- **History:** **1980–present (~45 years).** This is what powers genuine 40-year multivariate training in Earth Pulse.
- **Note:** ERA5 (Copernicus, 1940–present) can extend further but is not NASA; it is listed in the README as an allowed partner source.

chunks.title: 12. Partner / supplementary sources (from README)
chunks.text:
12. Partner / supplementary sources (from README)
| Source | What it adds | History |
|---|---|---|
| **USGS EarthExplorer (Landsat)** | Real historical **photos/scenes** of any place | 1972–present (practical continuous ~1984+) |
| **Copernicus CDS (ERA5)** | 5th-generation atmospheric reanalysis | **1940–present** |
| **NOAA NCEI** | Global weather/climate records, GHCN | varies |
| **Open-Meteo** | Free weather API, no key — forecast companion | recent years |
| **Global Forest Watch** | Forest loss/gain | ~2000–present |
| **JRC Global Surface Water** | Surface water occurrence change | ~1984–2021 |
| **OpenAQ** | Air quality | varies |
| **IMD / data.gov.in** | India-specific weather & open govt data | varies |
| **World Bank Open Data** | Country indicators | varies |
| **Hugging Face Hub** | Hosting trained models/datasets | n/a |
---

chunks.title: How much history can you honestly get? (the 40-year check)
chunks.text:
How much history can you honestly get? (the 40-year check)
| Parameter | Source | Realistic range |
|---|---|---|
| Air temperature / solar / humidity / wind / pressure (point) | NASA POWER | **~1981–present** |
| Consistent multivariate met (gridded) | MERRA-2 | **1980–present** |
| Global temperature anomaly context | GISTEMP | **1880–present** |
| Sea ice concentration | NSIDC | **~1979–present** (product-dependent) |
| Sea surface temperature | PO.DAAC MUR | ~2002–present |
| Sea level (altimetry) | PO.DAAC | ~1993–present |
| NDVI/EVI, LST, evapotranspiration, burned area | LP DAAC (MODIS) | **~2000–present** |
| Precipitation (satellite) | GPM IMERG / TRMM | ~2000–present |
| Fire hotspots | FIRMS | ~2000–present |
| Real-scene imagery | Landsat | 1972–present |

chunks.title: How much history can you honestly get? (the 40-year check)
chunks.text:
How much history can you honestly get? (the 40-year check)
**Bottom line:** a genuine **~40-year backbone** exists (MERRA-2 / NASA POWER / GISTEMP / NSIDC sea ice, plus ERA5 if you opt in). Modern-sensor parameters (NDVI, SST, sea level, fires) have **~20–25 years** — do not stretch them. The app always reports per-parameter coverage, trains multivariate models on the **overlap period**, and shows gaps instead of hiding them.
---

chunks.title: Practical fetch order used by Earth Pulse
chunks.text:
Practical fetch order used by Earth Pulse
1. **Tier A (on click, instant):** NASA POWER point series + GIBS imagery tiles + FIRMS events (if key) + precomputed gridded trends/forecasts. No login, no heavy downloads.
2. **Tier B (on demand, bounded):** `discover.py` queries CMR/OPeNDAP for the exact product coverage at that point; subsets and caches. Results are merged into the place payload with an explicit `data_coverage` report.
3. **Precompute (offline/CI):** the full globe is processed into a Zarr store by `pipeline/run_pipeline.py` + `engine/run_engine.py`; the API serves ready-made results keyed by grid cell.

chunks.title: High-resolution, real-data path — any place on Earth (Belgaum case study)
chunks.text:
High-resolution, real-data path — any place on Earth (Belgaum case study)
This document describes how Earth Pulse goes from the bundled 15° synthetic demo
to a **sub-kilometre, real-data** analysis for a single place, using
**Belgaum (Belagavi), Karnataka (15.8497 N, 74.4977 E)** as the showcase.

chunks.title: Works for any place on Earth
chunks.text:
Works for any place on Earth
The `/point` endpoint and `pipeline/fetch_highres_point.py` accept **any** lat/lon
(-90..90, -180..180). The frontend has a global place search (OpenStreetMap
Nominatim) plus a 📍 Belgaum shortcut; clicking anywhere on the map in
🛰 Hi-Res mode also triggers a high-res point build. Ocean points are handled
honestly (NDVI masked, SST/sea level reported as unavailable from POWER).

chunks.title: Resolution ladder
chunks.text:
Resolution ladder
| Product | Resolution | Period | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| NASA POWER (point API) | ~0.5° source, interpolated to point | 1981–present | temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, solar |
| MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI | 250 m, 16-day | 2000–present | vegetation greenness (via AppEEARS, Earthdata login) |
| GPM IMERG | 0.1°, 30-min | 2000–present | high-res precipitation (optional, Earthdata login) |
| Sentinel-2 L2A | 10 m | 2015–present | true-colour + NDVI imagery (Planetary Computer, no login) |
| Landsat 8/9 | 30 m | 2013–present | longer imagery archive (Planetary Computer, no login) |
| GIBS MODIS tiles | 250 m–1 km | 2000–present | map backdrop tiles |

chunks.title: Resolution ladder
chunks.text:
Resolution ladder
No single product gives 40 years at 0.5 km. Earth Pulse is honest about this:
POWER provides the 40-year climate record at point level; MODIS adds 250 m
vegetation since 2000; Sentinel-2 adds 10 m imagery since 2015. Forecasts are
probabilistic (p10–p90) and labeled as model outlooks, never as certain futures.

```bash
python3 scripts/build_belgaum.py
```

The web app has a **🛰 Hi-Res** toggle and a **📍 Belgaum** shortcut button.

chunks.title: Honest limits
chunks.text:
Honest limits
- POWER is satellite+model agroclimatology, not native 0.5 km.
- NDVI needs Earthdata login for 250 m; otherwise unavailable (never faked).
- SST/sea level are ocean variables; for an inland place like Belgaum they are
masked (NaN) and reported as unavailable.
- Forecasts are probabilistic p10–p90; the "next move" summary is a
direction/magnitude hint, not a prediction of discrete events.
- Scenario images are illustrative only.

chunks.title: Earth Pulse — honest limitations
chunks.text:
Earth Pulse — honest limitations
Read this before trusting any number the app shows. Every limitation below is
grounded in the code; citing it in the UI or demo is encouraged, not embarrassing.

chunks.title: 1. The bundled demo data is synthetic — not real observations
chunks.text:
1. The bundled demo data is synthetic — not real observations
- `data/samples/earth_pulse_sample.npz` is **generated by code**
(`pipeline/run_pipeline.py --sample` → `pipeline/export_store.py`), deterministic
and physically motivated, but it is **not measured data**.
- The trends are **baked in**: e.g., temperature warms, precipitation drifts, sea
level rises at 3.4 mm/yr, SST resumes +0.10 °C/decade — by construction. Demo
charts therefore *illustrate the app*, they do **not** quantify real climate.
- The store metadata says exactly this (`synthetic: true`,
`provenance: "synthetic_demo"`), and the API repeats it in
`data_coverage.synthetic_demo` + the explainer. Keep that label everywhere.

chunks.title: 2. Demo grid resolution is very coarse
chunks.text:
2. Demo grid resolution is very coarse
- The synthetic store is a **15° × 15°** grid: 10 latitudes (−60…75) × 24
longitudes (−180…165) = **240 cells**, 498 months (**1985-01 → 2026-06**).
- Clicking New York and Cape Town 15° apart can hit the same cell. Real products
would use 0.25°–1° resolution and a proper land/ocean mask.

chunks.title: 3. Real-data record lengths differ per parameter — never claim "40 years" for everything
chunks.text:
3. Real-data record lengths differ per parameter — never claim "40 years" for everything
See `docs/data-sources.md` for the full check. Bottom line:
| Record | Honest start |
|---|---|
| MERRA-2 / POWER backbone | ~1980 / ~1981 |
| GISTEMP anomaly context | 1880 |
| Sea ice (NSIDC) | ~1979 |
| MODIS NDVI/LST/fire | ~2000 (**~25 y**) |
| SST (MUR GHRSST) | ~2002 |
| Sea-level altimetry | ~1993 |
The app trains multivariate models only on the **overlap period** and reports
per-parameter coverage instead of hiding the differences.

chunks.title: 4. Forecast skill degrades with horizon
chunks.text:
4. Forecast skill degrades with horizon
- Default horizon is **60 months**; uncertainty bands inflate with √h
(residual σ·√h). Error bars grow, skill drops — the p10–p90 ribbon is a
*probabilistic outlook*, not a guarantee.
- The bands are calibrated on the data they were trained on (backtest PICP). The
real-POWER store has a genuine rolling-origin backtest, but it still covers one
region/horizon; the synthetic demo's PICP says nothing about real-world
coverage.
- Regime shifts (volcanic eruptions, ENSO flips, abrupt land-use change) are
outside the training distribution; the model cannot anticipate them.

chunks.title: 5. Regional teleconnections are unmodeled
chunks.text:
5. Regional teleconnections are unmodeled
- Features are per-parameter lags + month harmonics (sin/cos) + a year index.
ENSO, monsoon dynamics, ocean–atmosphere coupling and other teleconnections
have **no explicit representation** — "opposite trends" explanations are
generic, not mechanism-specific.

chunks.title: 6. Opposite Trend Detector is statistical, not causal
chunks.text:
6. Opposite Trend Detector is statistical, not causal
- It pairs neighbouring cells whose slopes have opposite signs and rates the
pair strong only when both Mann–Kendall tests are significant
(`engine/opposite.py`). It is a *detective lead*, not evidence of cause; it
says nothing about which mechanism (land use, irrigation, orography, local
pollution) drives the divergence.

chunks.title: 7. Climate twins are an arbitrary clustering
chunks.text:
7. Climate twins are an arbitrary clustering
- K-Means, k=8 (`configs/model.yaml`), z-scored multivariate cell features with a
fixed seed. Different k reassigns cells; clusters are a *didactic similarity
view*, not a recognized climate classification.

chunks.title: 8. Synthetic store ignores geography
chunks.text:
8. Synthetic store ignores geography
- No land/ocean/coast mask: SST and sea level are shown for inland cells
(symbolic). No elevation, land cover or irrigation variables per cell.

chunks.title: 9. Narration: local LLM is optional, guarded, and small
chunks.text:
9. Narration: local LLM is optional, guarded, and small
- `POST /chat` uses a **local Ollama** model (default `qwen2.5:1.5b`) when it is
running. `/place` explanations stay **templated** by default; set
`EP_EXPLAIN_LLM=1` to use Ollama there too (slower). If Ollama is unreachable,
both endpoints return deterministic templated prose instead of failing. - **HF Inference** (`HF_TOKEN`) is an optional alternate backend. The **Gemini**
backend is planned and **not yet wired** (`api/services/explainer.py`; key
already plumbed through `docker-compose.yml`). - The LLM only re-words backend facts; it never computes a statistic. A 1.5B
local model can still misread statistics, so post-generation guards reject
certainty claims, p-values framed as probabilities/confidence, p10–p90 bands
described as 10–90% chances, non-significant trends called significant, and
any number absent from the facts.

chunks.title: 9. Narration: local LLM is optional, guarded, and small
chunks.text:
9. Narration: local LLM is optional, guarded, and small
Rejected drafts are replaced with
`templated-guard` prose and report `guard_reason` / `guard_numbers`.

chunks.title: 10. Deployment/operational limits
chunks.text:
10. Deployment/operational limits
- API is read-mostly (`GET` plus `POST /explain` and `POST /chat`), in-process
rate limiting; no auth — built for demo scale, not hostile public traffic.
- Free tiers sleep (Render) or force cold rebuilds (HF Spaces); first request may
be slow.
- The web map pulls OSM/GIBS tiles from the network; low-bandwidth mode strips
imagery but MapLibre still needs connectivity for the base map.
- Watchlist/alerts live in `localStorage` only — no accounts, no server-side
notification transport.

chunks.title: 11. What the demo must never be claimed to be
chunks.text:
11. What the demo must never be claimed to be
- A measurements product, an operational forecast, a peer-reviewed study, or an
attribution tool. It is an **open educational explorer** with honest labels:
*Observed* (real sources, when wired) · *Model forecast (p10–p90)* ·
*Synthetic demo* · *AI-generated scenario* (disabled by default).

chunks.title: ML / AI layers — models, inputs, outputs, failure modes
chunks.text:
ML / AI layers — models, inputs, outputs, failure modes
Earth Pulse uses the right tool per layer. Numbers are computed by statistics/ML; the LLM only narrates structured facts and is templated-fallback capable. Accuracy = probabilistic skill + honest coverage — never vibes.

chunks.title: 1. Trend estimation (per grid cell, per parameter)
chunks.text:
1. Trend estimation (per grid cell, per parameter)
- **Method:** Theil–Sen slope (median of all pairwise slopes) + **Mann–Kendall** test (S, normal approximation w/ tie correction, two-sided p).
- **Why:** ordinary least squares is wrecked by outliers/gaps; Theil–Sen is robust; MK gives a significance for "is this really changing?".
- **Output:** `{ slope_per_decade, p_value, significant, direction }` per cell/parameter.
- **Code:** `engine/trends.py`, precomputed by `engine/run_engine.py` → `data/processed/analysis.json`.

chunks.title: 2. Opposite Trend Detector (signature feature)
chunks.text:
2. Opposite Trend Detector (signature feature)
- **Method:** grid neighbor graph (radius = `neighbor_radius_grid_steps`, default 1). For each parameter, flag neighbor pairs whose slopes have opposite signs; if both are Mann–Kendall significant → `strength: strong`, otherwise `weak`. Rank by min(|slope_a|, |slope_b|).
- **Why:** surfaces divergence across neighboring places (e.g., one drying, one greening) — the "case file" for the detective UI.
- **Output:** `[{ parameter, cell_a, cell_b, strength, context_note }]`.
- **Code:** `engine/opposite.py`.

chunks.title: 3. Climate twins (clustering)
chunks.text:
3. Climate twins (clustering)
- **Method:** standardize (z-score) the per-cell multivariate vector `[temperature, precipitation, ndvi, sst]` (+ optional `sea_level`), then **K-Means** (NumPy implementation, seeded, k=8).
- **Note:** HDBSCAN is listed in `configs/model.yaml` as a pluggable option but is **not installed** and has no implementation path in the shipped code.
- **Output:** cluster id per cell; UI shows "places with the same climate signature".
- **Code:** `engine/climate_twins.py`.

chunks.title: 4. Forecasting (multivariate, with uncertainty)
chunks.text:
4. Forecasting (multivariate, with uncertainty)
- **Implemented (used by default):** `models/forecast.py::RidgeRollout` — closed-form ridge regression on lag features, autoregressive roll-out, residual-based p10/p50/p90 bands inflated by √h. Works offline, trains in seconds.
- **LSTM / PyTorch:** `models/forecast.py` contains a `LSTMForecaster` **class stub** only. It is **never instantiated, trained, or saved** by `models/train.py`. The `--torch` flag in `train.py` is parsed but has no effect. The Colab notebook (`notebooks/02_train_forecast.ipynb`) is a **demo**, not a trained artifact. Treat LSTM as **unimplemented**.
- **Features:** flattened 24-month windows of all parameters (`prepare_cell_matrix`). No lat/lon features are added in the current implementation.
- **Horizon:** 60 months (5 years) default.

chunks.title: 4. Forecasting (multivariate, with uncertainty)
chunks.text:
4. Forecasting (multivariate, with uncertainty)
- **Uncertainty:** residual σ·√h widening per step. PicP ≥ 0.80 at 80% nominal is a **target**, not an enforced assertion — measured backtest PICP is 96–100% on the synthetic store.
- **Evaluation:** rolling-origin backtest (`models/backtest.py`) vs persistence & seasonal-naive & linear-trend baselines. Run on the synthetic store; PicP on synthetic data is not indicative of real-world coverage.
- **Code:** `models/forecast.py`, `models/dataset.py`, `models/backtest.py`, `models/train.py`, `models/infer.py`.

chunks.title: 5. Anomaly detection
chunks.text:
5. Anomaly detection
- **Method:** **rolling robust z-score** `(x − rolling_median) / (1.4826 · rolling_MAD)`, window 61 months, |z| ≥ 3.5 → flag. `models/anomaly.py` implements only this. The Isolation Forest backend listed in `configs/model.yaml` is **not wired** into `api/routers/place.py` today.
- **Output:** `{ parameter, date, z, severity (moderate|high), kind }`.
- **Code:** `models/anomaly.py`.

chunks.title: 6. Explainable narrative (LLM)
chunks.text:
6. Explainable narrative (LLM)
- **Method:** facts-only prompt (numbers, coverage, uncertainty) → short plain-English paragraph. Implemented backends: **templated** (offline, always works) and **HF Inference API** (`HF_TOKEN`) — both in `api/services/explainer.py`.
- **Not wired:** a **Gemini** backend is referenced in docs but is **not implemented** in the codebase.
- The LLM only words numbers; it never computes them.
- **Code:** `api/services/explainer.py`.

chunks.title: 7. “Future image” — what it honest & what it isn't
chunks.text:
7. “Future image” — what it honest & what it isn't
- **Default & honest:** `models/project_maps.py` renders **SVG heat-maps** of model-projected parameter fields (Theil–Sen extrapolation). URL: `GET /imagery/projected?parameter=temperature&year=2030`.
- **Optional & labeled:** `models/scenario_image.py` — conditioned diffusion image-to-image for lower/median/upper scenario cards. **Must** display "AI-generated scenario — not an observation."
- **Feature exists:** `models/scenario_cards.py` CLI can generate PNGs offline with a GPU (or CPU with SD-Turbo). `api/routers/scenario.py` exposes conditioning-only via HTTP.
- **But** `configs/model.yaml → scenario_image.enabled` is set to `true` in this repo because the pipeline is working; the doc’s “disabled by default” was the intended safe default, not the current state.
- **Past photos:** GIBS tiles (`pipeline/fetch_gibs.py`) + USGS EarthExplorer link for Landsat scene-level imagery.

chunks.title: Real data (not synthetic)
chunks.text:
Real data (not synthetic)
- The API serves the **real NASA POWER store by default** when `data/processed/earth_pulse_power_real.npz` exists.
- **NDVI / SST / sea level are absent** from POWER and are shown as "No coverage" in the UI — never faked. Hi-Res `/point` mode fills NDVI from Sentinel-2 (10m, no login).
- Real-store backtest Artifact: `models/artifacts/forecaster_real.npz` (trained on 126,480 real pooled windows). The grid-mode ridge artifact `forecaster.npz` is the same architecture but was trained on the synthetic store — if you want real-grid forecasts, set `EP_STORE_PATH=data/processed/earth_pulse_power_real.npz`.

chunks.title: Known failure modes (be honest in the UI)
chunks.text:
Known failure modes (be honest in the UI)
- Regime shifts outside the training distribution (e.g., volcanic aerosol, abrupt land-use change).
- Cross-sensor bias when stitching TRMM↔GPM or MODIS↔VIIRS.
- Static coast/ocean masks are ignored in the synthetic store (SST shown inland is symbolic).
- Extrapolation inflates p10/p90 optimistically — always show band width and backtest PicP.
- Synthetic-train PicP=96-100% says nothing about real-world skill.

chunks.title: Real data run — NASA POWER store (built & verified)
chunks.text:
Real data run — NASA POWER store (built & verified)

chunks.title: What it is
chunks.text:
What it is
A **real, measured/modelled** multivariate store (1981-01 → 2026-11, monthly) covering the demo grid:

chunks.title: Verified results (real output, not claims)
chunks.text:
Verified results (real output, not claims)
- `synthetic_demo: false` in `data_coverage`; `provenance: nasa_power_monthly_1981_present`

Serving it vs the demo
| | Demo (default) | Real POWER |
|---|---|---|
| Store | synthetic (labeled) | `earth_pulse_power_real.npz` (labeled real) |
| `make sample-data engine train test` | ✓ works | point `EP_STORE_PATH`/`EP_ANALYSIS_PATH` at the real artifacts |

chunks.title: What this is NOT
chunks.text:
What this is NOT
- POWER is **satellite+model agroclimatology** (CERES/GEOS-class), not raw native satellite — excellent for a free 40-year record, slightly conservative vs raw in-situ/reanalysis (see docs/limitations.md).
- NDVI/SST/sea level still need **Earthdata login** (MODIS/PO.DAAC) — see `docs/real-data-ingestion.md`; the POWER path is the no-credentials real-data backbone.
- 15°×15° grid is illustrative; production → 1° (same code, ~4000× more cells — watch memory on the monthly chunks).

chunks.title: From synthetic demo → real NASA data (end-to-end)
chunks.text:
From synthetic demo → real NASA data (end-to-end)
The repo ships a deterministic synthetic store so everything runs offline. This guide flips it to real NASA products with **no code changes** — only environment variables and one ingestion run.

chunks.title: What changes
chunks.text:
What changes
| Piece | Synthetic (default) | Real data |
|---|---|---|
| Store | `data/samples/earth_pulse_sample.npz` (7.4 MB, deterministic) | Zarr store from `pipeline/run_pipeline.py --gridded` |
| Mask | Embedded 15° dominant-class mask (`pipeline/land_ocean.py`) | Derived: ocean where SST is finite ≥50% of climatology |
| `data_coverage.synthetic_demo` | `true` | `false` (auto) |
| `synthetic_demo` labels in UI/API | shown | gone |

Prerequisites

chunks.title: Step 1 — Real ingestion (Tier B / batch)
chunks.text:
Step 1 — Real ingestion (Tier B / batch)
`pipeline/fetch_gridded.py` (already in repo) discovers granules via earthaccess and opens them with xarray; subset to monthly, to a bounding box or point:

chunks.title: Step 1 — Real ingestion (Tier B / batch)
chunks.text:
Step 1 — Real ingestion (Tier B / batch)

Design rules (enforced in code)
1. OFF unless `configs/model.yaml → scenario_image.enabled: true` **or** `EP_SCENARIO_IMAGES=1`.
2. Every call must pass `acknowledge_not_observation=True` (CLI sets it; HTTP never generates).

4. Negative prompt bans text/borders/people/fake buildings; geography (coastline, rivers, roads, settlements) must be preserved; only land-cover color balance shifts.
5. Strength: lower 0.25 / median 0.35 / upper 0.45 — lower variants are nearer the source tile, so they are conservative.

chunks.title: NASA POWER primer (curated summary)
chunks.text:
NASA POWER primer (curated summary)
Curated by the Earth Pulse team from NASA's public documentation. This is a
plain-English summary for the chatbot's knowledge base, not an official NASA
text. When in doubt, consult the official source: https://power.larc.nasa.gov

chunks.title: What NASA POWER is
chunks.text:
What NASA POWER is
NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) provides solar and
meteorological time series for renewable-energy, building, and agroclimatology
applications. It fuses satellite observations and model reanalysis into a
analysis-ready monthly (and daily) time series, distributed free of charge via
the POWER API, with no login required for most parameters.

chunks.title: Why Earth Pulse uses it
chunks.text:
Why Earth Pulse uses it
- Free, open, reproducible — matches the project's open-data rule.
- Monthly resolution matches the app's trend detection (Theil–Sen + Mann–Kendall).
- Long record: the MERRA-2-based backbone starts around 1980/1981, which is
enough for 40+ years of trend estimation per cell — but per-parameter
coverage still differs and must always be reported, never assumed.

chunks.title: Parameters NASA POWER provides (used by Earth Pulse)
chunks.text:
Parameters NASA POWER provides (used by Earth Pulse)
- Temperature (T2M): 2-meter air temperature, in °C.
- Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR): bias-corrected total precipitation, mm/month (or mm/day in daily products).
- Solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN): all-sky surface shortwave downward irradiance; POWER publishes Wh/m²/day or kWh/m²/day depending on community (Earth Pulse uses community=RE, metric, kWh/m²/day).
- Relative humidity (RH2M): 2-meter relative humidity, %.
- Wind speed (WS2M): 2-meter wind speed, m/s.

chunks.title: What NASA POWER does NOT provide
chunks.text:
What NASA POWER does NOT provide
- NDVI / vegetation index — use MODIS/VIIRS via LP DAAC (~2000–present), not POWER.
- Sea surface temperature — use PO.DAAC / MUR GHRSST (~2002–present), not POWER.
- Sea-level height — use altimetry products (~1993–present), not POWER.
Earth Pulse reports these as **unavailable** at POWER-backed cells rather than
inventing values.

chunks.title: Grid and resolution
chunks.text:
Grid and resolution
The POWER community=RE native grid is roughly 0.5° × 0.625°. Earth Pulse ships
an illustrative 15° × 15° grid (10 latitudes × 24 longitudes = 240 cells) so
the hackathon build stays small and fast; the finest click point is the
nearest 15° cell center, not sub-cell truth. Real deployments should regrid to
the native POWER resolution or finer.

chunks.title: Community, units and access
chunks.text:
Community, units and access
- Community: RE (renewable energy) is the default for agroclimatology use in Earth Pulse.
- Access: HTTPS API at power.larc.nasa.gov — no key required. `pipeline/fetch_power.py` shows the request pattern used here.
- Provenance string in the store metadata: `nasa_power_monthly_1981_present`.

chunks.title: Honest caveats
chunks.text:
Honest caveats
- POWER is satellite+model agroclimatology, not a physical weather station at your exact location.
- Parameter record lengths differ; "1981–present" applies to the POWER backbone, not to MODIS-era parameters.
- POWER monthly values are regional/point agroclimatology; local microclimates differ.
- Trend estimates are statistical associations in the record, not causal attribution to human activity.

chunks.title: Earth Pulse methodology (method notes)
chunks.text:
Earth Pulse methodology (method notes)
How the numbers shown in Earth Pulse are produced. Written for the chatbot's
knowledge base; grounded in this repository's code (`engine/trends.py`,
`models/anomaly.py`, `models/forecast.py`, `engine/climate_twins.py`,
`engine/opposite.py`, `api/services/explainer.py`).

chunks.title: Trend estimation: Theil–Sen + Mann–Kendall
chunks.text:
Trend estimation: Theil–Sen + Mann–Kendall
- Slope per decade is the Theil–Sen median-of-pairwise-slopes estimator — robust to outliers.
- Significance is the Mann–Kendall p-value on the monthly record. p < 0.05 is the conventional threshold for calling a trend "statistically significant".
- A non-significant p-value does NOT prove there is no change — it means the data cannot confirm one at that threshold.
- A p-value is not a confidence level, probability, or certainty. Never state "100% certain" or convert p into a percentage of confidence.
- Roughly 40–45 years of monthly data (~500 points) is what each cell carries; shorter records widen p-values.

chunks.title: Anomalies: rolling robust z-score
chunks.text:
Anomalies: rolling robust z-score
- Each month is compared against a rolling seasonal window (61 months) using a modified robust z-score (median/MAD-based).
- |z| ≥ 3.5 flags an "unusual month". Anomalies are temporary departures from the seasonal cycle, not proof of a permanent regime shift or a disaster.
- Earth Pulse reports the count and the largest departures; it does not attribute causes.

chunks.title: Forecasting: ridge rollout with p10–p90 bands
chunks.text:
Forecasting: ridge rollout with p10–p90 bands
- Features: per-parameter lags + month harmonics (sin/cos) + a year index; a ridge model rolls forward month by month.
- Forecasts are probabilistic outlooks with p10–p90 bands. The band widens with horizon (√h growth of residual σ).
- The reported "delta" in `/chat` facts is the TOTAL NET CHANGE from the first to the last forecast month — it is NOT a per-decade rate.
- Backtest skill (MAE/RMSE/PICP) is reported per parameter in the /place payload when a trained artifact is available. PICP = prediction interval coverage probability (should sit near 80% for a calibrated p10–p90 band).
- Regime shifts (volcanoes, abrupt ENSO flips, land-use change) are outside the training distribution and are not anticipated.

chunks.title: Climate twins: K-Means over cell fingerprints
chunks.text:
Climate twins: K-Means over cell fingerprints
- Cells are clustered (k=8) on z-scored multivariate features. Clusters are a didactic similarity view, not a recognized climate classification; different k reassigns cells.
- A "twin" is a hypothesis for cross-region comparison, not proof of shared causes. Compare dataset resolution and coverage before claims.

chunks.title: Opposite trends: statistical dipoles, not causation
chunks.text:
Opposite trends: statistical dipoles, not causation
- Pairs of neighbouring cells with opposite-sign slopes; marked "strong" only when both Mann–Kendall tests are significant.
- This is a detective lead. Mechanisms (irrigation, land use, orography, microclimate) need local evidence.

chunks.title: Facts-locked narration (why the chatbot is careful)
chunks.text:
Facts-locked narration (why the chatbot is careful)
- The LLM never computes or changes numbers. Backend code assembles a FACTS dict (trends, forecast deltas, anomalies, coverage); the LLM only re-words it.
- Post-generation guards reject: certainty claims, p-values framed as probabilities/confidence, p10–p90 bands described as a "10–90% chance", non-significant trends called significant, and numbers that do not appear in the facts (no model arithmetic allowed).
- Failing any guard substitutes deterministic templated prose (generator `templated-guard`) instead of publishing a false claim.

chunks.title: RAG design (what retrieval adds)
chunks.text:
RAG design (what retrieval adds)
- Retrieval adds CONTEXT (domain docs, method notes, data-coverage facts) next to FACTS (the cell's actual numbers).
- Facts still win on conflict: the prompt instructs the model that FACTS SUMMARY overrides CONTEXT; guards still run on the output.
- Citations: sources used are returned as [S1], [S2] … and shown in the chat UI as a "Sources" line.
